findings.title: Task 6 breaks the existing package test that expects exactly three tools, and no task updates it
findings.description: `test_exactly_the_three_builtin_tools_are_registered` checks `set(tools.list_tools()) == {"read_file", "write_file", "bash"}` (line 11). `test_materialize_binds_every_registered_tool` checks `len(executors) == 3` (line 22). Task 6.4 (task file lines 210-212) registers five more tools when `squadron.tools` is imported, so both tests fail at the Task 6 commit. That contradicts "Each task leaves the suite green" (line 55). The context summary (lines 50-51) says the builtin names are "read via `tools.list_tools()`, never hard-coded", but that is wrong for this file. Task 6 never mentions `test_package.py`, and Task 7 creates a new file without touching it. Fix: Task 6 should update both assertions (to the eight-name set and `len == 8`, or to builtins ⊆ registered). Task 6's success criterion at line 217 already says "five `cf_*` plus three builtins", so the edit should go there.

findings.title: The CI runner has node and an initialized CF project, so the live contract test will run in CI, not skip
findings.description:
Task 8.1 (lines 256-259) and the slice (line 215) assume "CI without node stays green". But `ci.yml` installs Node 22 (lines 20-22), installs `@context-forge/cli` and runs `cf init --lite --no-ide` (lines 23-24) before `uv run pytest` (line 32). So the default `npx -y @context-forge/mcp` will launch, and the gate in Task 8.1 will not skip. As a result, every CI run would:
- download the latest, unpinned MCP package from npm
- run the drift assertions, so a CF release that renames an argument turns squadron CI red
- run the 8.2 round-trip, whose expectation ("content mentioning the project", line 267) depends on whatever `cf init --lite` registers

That may be acceptable as drift defense, but the plan should choose it on purpose. Task 8 should:
- say whether CI is expected to run this test
- apply the existing `network` marker (`pyproject.toml:83-85`), since npx fetches from the network
- make 8.2's assertion hold for the project CI initializes, or skip 8.2 outside a developer checkout

findings.title: Config-read and command-parse failures can raise out of the executor
findings.description: Task 6.3 (lines 205-207) reads `cf.mcp_timeout_s` through `get_typed_config`, which raises `ValueError` on a type mismatch (manager.py:103-105). For example, a TOML file can hold `cf.mcp_timeout_s = "60"`. `get_config` returns `object`, so a non-string `cf.mcp_command` from TOML is possible. `shlex.split` raises `ValueError` on an unbalanced quote. An empty string splits to `[]`, which leaves no command to pass to `StdioServerParameters`. Each of these escapes the executor, which breaks the "errors are values" contract (fact 2, line 29; slice line 149). Nothing in Task 6.3 handles them, and Task 7.3 does not test them. Add a step that turns config and parse failures into `ToolResult(is_error=True)` with a WARNING, plus one test (for example, an unbalanced-quote command).

findings.title: No test covers the protocol/transport failure-mode row
findings.description: The slice says "Each row above has a test asserting the observable signal" (slice lines 149-150). One of those rows is "Protocol/transport error mid-call (`McpError`, closed stream)" (line 146). Task 4.3 implements it (line 143), but neither 5.4 (lines 173-176, which lists timeout, isError and spawn failure only) nor the fixture in 3.1 covers it. Add a `crash` tool to the fake server (for example `os._exit(1)` mid-call) and a test in 5.4 that asserts `is_error` plus the WARNING.

findings.title: Two result-mapping rules have no tests (part of success criterion 2)
findings.description:
Success criterion 2 (slice lines 221-222) requires results mapped "per the Result mapping rules". Two of those rules are untested:
- **Multiple text blocks joined with `\n`:** Task 4.2 implements it (line 134), but the `echo` tool returns a single block, so the join is never exercised.
- **Non-text blocks noted by type:** Task 4.2 implements it (line 137), but no fixture tool returns an image or resource block.

Add a fake-server tool that returns two text blocks plus one `ImageContent`, and one test in Task 5.1 for it.

findings.title: The timeout test does not actually check process-group teardown
findings.description:
Fact 6 (lines 42-45) says the grandchild reaping must be asserted in the timeout test. Task 5.2 (lines 167-169) only checks that the direct child PID is gone, then claims "this pins the SDK process-group teardown fact". Killing only the direct child would also pass that check, so a regression to non-group kill would go undetected. That non-group kill is exactly the orphaned `npx` → `node` risk. Also, the Task 3.1 fixture spec (lines 102-111) has no PID-reporting behavior, so Task 5 would have to change a fixture committed in an earlier task.

Fix:
- In Task 3, have the `sleep` tool spawn a grandchild (for example `subprocess.Popen([sys.executable, "-c", "import time; time.sleep(60)"])`).
- Have the fixture write both PIDs to a path passed as a server argument.
- In 5.2, assert both PIDs are gone.

findings.title: Env handling is assigned to both the bridge and the caller, and the two descriptions conflict
findings.description: Task 4.1 (lines 129-131) says the bridge uses `get_default_environment()` as the spawned process env, and also that "callers construct `StdioServerParameters`". Task 6.3 (line 207) has the caller pass `env=get_default_environment()` as well. If the bridge overrides `server.env`, caller-supplied env is silently lost, which breaks the 5.2 option of telling the fake server its PID file through env. Pick one owner. The simplest choice: the bridge passes `server` through unchanged, and only the caller sets `env`.

findings.title: The `mcp>=1.0.0` dependency floor allows SDK versions without the behavior the design relies on
findings.description: The plan relies on mcp 1.26.0 behavior: `StdioServerParameters.cwd`, `start_new_session=True` and `os.killpg` teardown (fact 6, lines 42-45; slice lines 32-33, 152-157). `uv.lock` pins 1.26.0, but `pyproject.toml` allows `mcp>=1.0.0`, and squadron is published to PyPI (`ci.yml:34-53`). An installation that resolves an older mcp could ignore or reject `cwd`, and project identity comes from that `cwd` (slice Security section, lines 174-177). It could also orphan servers. Add a step in Task 4 that raises the floor to the version the design checked (`mcp>=1.26`).

findings.title: Commits come after every task, so implementation is committed before it is tested
findings.description: Every task, 1 through 9, ends with its own commit (lines 84, 96, 120, 152, 182, 220, 251, 274, 299). Tasks 1, 4 and 6 commit implementation that is not yet tested, and the Task 6 commit is red (see the FAIL finding). Task 1 and Task 2 are also too finely split: two config keys and two default tests take two tasks and two commits. Merge 1+2 into one task, and place commit points after 2, 5 and 7, where each implementation lands together with its tests.

findings.title: Config tests need the `patch_config_paths` fixture, which the tasks don't mention
findings.description: Task 2 (`test_cf_mcp_timeout_default` reads through `get_typed_config`, line 91) and Task 7.3 (setting `cf.mcp_command`, lines 241-243) both read or write real config files unless they use `patch_config_paths`. The existing pattern is in `tests/config/test_keys.py:79-97`. Without the fixture, the tests depend on the developer's own config, and Task 7.3 would write to it. Task 6.3 also doesn't say which `cwd` to pass to `get_config`. Passing the bound `cwd` makes project-level `.squadron.toml` apply to the target project. Leaving the default `"."` uses the process CWD. State which one is intended.

findings.title: The timeout test's time bound must allow for the SDK's 2s termination grace
findings.description: Task 5.2 asks for `is_error` "within ~timeout wall-clock" (line 166), and Task 5's success criteria say "no test sleeps longer than a few seconds" (line 181). The design notes the SDK waits about 2s before escalating (slice line 154), so the call returns at about timeout + 2s. Give an explicit bound (for example `< timeout_s + 4`) so an implementer doesn't write a check that fails intermittently.

findings.title: Importing `squadron.tools` now pulls in the mcp SDK; the package docstring needs updating
findings.description: The package docstring says importing it "registers the built-in tools and does nothing else". `validate_allowed_tools` imports `squadron.tools` lazily on purpose to keep import order stable (`src/squadron/pipeline/steps/utils.py:66-69`). After Task 6.4, every pipeline validation also imports `mcp.client.stdio` and its pydantic/anyio dependencies. Task 6.4 should update the docstring. It should also say whether `mcp` imports belong inside `call_mcp_tool` (lazy) or at module scope.

findings.title: Success criterion 6's live model demo is deferred while the slice is marked complete
findings.description: Task 9.3 (lines 289-292) marks the slice `status: complete` while walkthrough step 4, the second half of success criterion 6, stays open. This follows the 263 precedent (263 is `status: complete`), and the `CLAUDECODE` guard is real (`src/squadron/cli/commands/run.py:148`). The deferral is stated openly, which is acceptable, but it should be recorded somewhere trackable, not only in the DEVLOG.

findings.title: Walkthrough step 3 deletes any existing user-level `cf.mcp_command` override
findings.description: Task 9.1 step 3 (line 283) sets and then unsets `cf.mcp_command` in the user config. If the developer already had a local-dev override (the slice's own example, line 165), `unset` removes it instead of restoring it. Use `--project` in a scratch directory, or record the previous value first and restore it afterwards.

findings.title: The Task 9.2 gates differ from what CI runs
findings.description: CI also runs `ruff format --check` and `cf validate frontmatter`. Task 9.3 edits the frontmatter of the task and slice files (`status: complete`), so add `cf validate frontmatter` to Task 9.2.

findings.title: No load test or CI gating task is needed
findings.description: The slice restates no performance or load requirement. The timeout is a correctness guard set by config, not a throughput target, so no `tests/load/` or CI gating task is required.

findings.title: Sequencing and layering are sound
findings.description: Config comes before the descriptors that read it, the fixture comes before the bridge tests, the bridge comes before the descriptors, and the live test comes last. There are no circular dependencies. The one-way `cf_tools` → `mcp_bridge` layering is checked at Task 6 (line 219). The live test reuses the constants as the single source (line 273).
